pk.context: 750 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: iron gray body and light green cap, opaque capsule

tell: A boxed rodent carcinogenicity warning and a 1963 first approval set this nitroimidazole antimicrobial apart.

clues.text: Food does not change how much is absorbed. Less than 20% is bound to plasma proteins, and urine carries 60% to 80% of the dose.
A synthetic compound with a molecular weight of 171.15 for the active moiety.
Approved under an NDA as 375 mg oral capsules, supplied in cartons of 100 unit doses.

Boxed warning that it is carcinogenic in mice and rats, so use is limited to the labeled conditions. Not to be given to anyone who took disulfiram in the last two weeks; nausea and headache are the most common reactions.
Trichomoniasis caused by T. vaginalis, symptomatic or asymptomatic, in females and males, plus treatment of asymptomatic sexual partners.
A synthetic nitroimidazole; the label gives no mechanism, only in vitro activity against most anaerobic bacteria and against trichomonads.
The generic name begins with M and has thirteen letters.
